newsitem.title: USA: Interior Department expects redwoods pact soon.
newsitem.headline: Interior Department expects redwoods pact soon.

text.p: Deputy Interior Secretary John Garamendi said he expected a "definitive" result Friday in negotiations to prevent the logging of thousands of acres of ancient northern California redwoods.

"I expect something definitive today," he said as he entered the office of Sen. Dianne Feinstein, a California Democrat. Negotiators were struggling against a deadline that permits logging in the virgin forests to begin Monday without an agreement.

Garamdeni was negotiating with Feinstein, California State Resources Secretary Doug Wheeler and Charles Hurwitz, the Texas financier who heads MAXXAM Inc., an energy company that owns the land in rural Humboldt County.
They met for 5 1/2 hours Thursday and resumed at about 9 a.m. Friday. Their attorneys were augmented by a lawyer from the Department of Justice's environmental unit.

Pacific Lumber Co., a unit of MAXXAM, agreed to delay the start of logging for two weeks in the virgin 3,000-acre (1,200-hectare) Headwaters area and five smaller groves. They said they would take only dead trees at first, but that would disturb the ecosystem in the virgin forest, environmentalists said.

Environmentalists argue that 60,000 acres (24,000 hectares) of the area should be protected, saying it encompasses an ecosystem needed to preserve endangered fish and birds. But the negotiations center on the Headwaters area, a buffer zone of 1,500 acres (600 hectares) and about 1,800 to 3,000 acres (700-1,200 hectares) included in the other parcels.
